core_obligations: Apply the descent statement for quasi-compact opens to find a finite subextension k' and an open V' over k' pulling back to V, which is part (1) (proof lines 891-893).
Observe that the Galois group of the extension over k' is an open subgroup of the full Galois group and that its elements fix V, which is part (2) (proof lines 893-895).
proof_roadmap: Descent to a finite subextension (proof lines 891-893).
Open stabilizer from the Galois correspondence (proof lines 893-895).
difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over k, a possibly infinite Galois extension and a quasi-compact open V of the base change, the lemma shows that V descends to a quasi-compact open over some finite subextension and that its stabilizer contains an open subgroup of the Galois group (statement lines 876-889). The proof obtains the descent from the general descent statement for quasi-compact opens along a finitely generated subalgebra, which gives part (1), and then observes that the Galois group of the extension over the finite subextension is open in the full Galois group, so its elements fix the descended open and part (2) follows (proof lines 891-895). The claim is H2: one descent input plus a one-line observation on the topology of the Galois group, with the passage from the subalgebra statement to the finite subextension being immediate in this setting.
